resources.string:
1. Check the match number and the position assigned to you on the scouting schedule. 
 	 2. Enter your name, the robot number, robot position, and the human player position. 
 	 3. Start in the Auto section. 
 	 4. Watch your assigned robot, filling out the fields associated with your robot's actions. 
 	 5. When the first bell rings, go to the Tele-Op section. 
 	 6. Repeat step 4. 
 	 7. When the game is over, go to the Endgame section and fill out the boxes. 
 	 8. Go to the Notes section, and input any notes. 
 	 9. Click the 3 lines on the right, and select submit.

• Some helpful piece of text related to the game. 
 	 • Examples of things to put in the notes box: Broken autos or negative elements of match that hinder the robots ability to perform
 	 • How to count. Instead of counting every single ball, find groups of 5 and use the + 5 button to add five. This year's game isn’t about precise accuracy, it’s about approximation.

• FUEL= The abundant yellow game piece that are shot into the HUB 
 	 • OUTPOST = Where the robot can get FUEL from a human player 
 	 • DEPOT = A 24 FUEL storage area that DOES NOT refill 
 	 • TOWER = The ladder that the robot climbs during ENDGAME and AUTO 
 	 • HUB = A large structure where FUEL is scored in during its ALLIANCE PERIOD 
 	 • ALLIANCE PERIOD = The 25 seconds when the HUB is active and can be scored in 
 	 • TRENCH = A structure that blocks tall robots from entering the center 
 	 • BUMP= Speed bump obstacle between the TRENCH and HUB that makes it harder for robots to cross the field

• If a robot does a penalty, the ref closest to them will wave the alliance team color flag 
 	 • The OUTPOST has a storage limit. Off-FIELD FUEL may only be stored in the CHUTE and the CORRAL. Excess FUEL, defined as the CHUTE and CORRAL being full, must immediately be entered onto the FIELD. 
 	 • DISABLED is when a robot is commanded to cease all operations for the round 
 	 • MINOR FOULS get the opposing team 5 extra points to their total 
 	 • MAJOR FOULS get the opposing team 15 extra points to their total 
 	 • YELLOW CARDS are issued for robot or team misconduct, including egregious/unsportsmanlike behavior and rule breaking 
 	 • RED CARDS are issues for a second yellow card, and DISQUALIFIES a team for the match

• Once a team receives a YELLOW or RED CARD, a yellow rectangle will show next to the team number on the audience display. 
 	 • Each alliance has their team numbers posted at the top of their color alliance 
 	 • ENERGIZED Ranking Point progress is displayed out of 100 under each alliance’s team numbers 
 	 • When ENERGIZED RP is completed, the counter goes up to 360 and that alliance is eligible for the SUPERCHARGED ranking point 
 	 • A yellow arrow icon will display on the alliance with an active Hub 
 	 • During Tele-Op, the amount of Hub shifts that have occurred and the amount of time left in the current shift are located above the match time
